label: github pull request
title: {org}/{repo}#{num} {title}
prompt:
Review the pull request at {url}.

The worktree is already on its branch. Read the diff against the base branch first, then the description, then the discussion. Report what you would block on and what is only a preference.
notes: A trailing path, query or fragment is allowed on purpose. .../pull/5/files and .../pull/5 are the same pull request. A path in front of /pull, or letters glued to the number, is not a pull request and does not match.

label: github issue
title: {org}/{repo}#{num} {title}
notes: An issue has no branch of its own, so the branch is named for the issue and the worktree is one you make before starting.

label: github branch
title: {org}/{repo} {ref}
prompt:
Continue the work on branch {ref} of {org}/{repo} ({url}).

Read the log against the default branch first, then say what the branch is doing and what looks unfinished.
notes: A tree url can also carry a folder after the branch, and the url alone cannot say where the branch name stops. The whole tail is taken as the branch, so paste the branch page, not a folder in it. Every segment starts with a letter, digit, _ or -, so no segment is . or .. and the worktree path cannot climb out.

label: a repository on github
title: {org}/{repo}
notes: THE SHRUG, and it belongs at the bottom. A url on a host we know that matches nothing more specific still gets a dialog, pointed at the clone. Refusing would be correct and useless.
